evidence: Column header is 'P1[Avg(?)]' or 'P1[Max(?)]', matching the 'P1' point marker visible on the IR camera screenshots reproduced in the paper's Figure 10 (which reads temperatures like 77.6C/85.3C/90.6C at a point labelled P1, and Figure 11's x-axis is literally 'Sample Point (Uniform Interval)', not time). Row counts (7-103) are the right order of magnitude to match individual .irgd clip frame counts (12-31 observed), suggesting each data#_avg.csv is a single-point trace extracted from one .irgd clip using third-party 'Sonel' radiometric-analysis software.

'Number' (1..N) is the only reliable sequence index and is NOT a trial number. There is no filename correspondence between data#_avg.csv and IRI_V_*.irgd (27 CSVs vs 28 irgd clips), so which P1 trace belongs to which irgd clip, which trial, or which material is unrecorded. Even if that link were established, P1 is a single ROI point, not a spatial field, so by itself it cannot populate the 6-zone 2D temperature arrays the pipeline's zone graph expects; a full-frame radiometric re-export from the original .irgd files (via Sonel or an equivalent decoder, with documented emissivity/reflected-temperature calibration) would be required for that.
